name: Apache Airflow
summary: A workflow platform that represents work as DAGs, stores task and workflow state in a metadata database, and uses a scheduler with pluggable executors to dispatch task instances.

features.name: DAG dependency graph
features.description: Airflow represents a workflow as a directed acyclic graph of tasks, where dependencies define the order in which task instances become eligible to run.
benefits: Makes workflow ordering and fan-in/fan-out explicit
Supports repeated runs of the same workflow definition
costs: The acyclic model cannot directly represent unbounded cyclic control flow
Complex dependency graphs increase scheduling and operational complexity

lifecycle.notes: The fixed official documentation and source directly record DAG task dependencies and readiness behavior for the cited Airflow revision.

features.name: Scheduler and metadata state
features.description: The scheduler triggers workflows, submits task instances to an executor, and coordinates through a metadata database that stores DAG, task, and variable state.
benefits: Centralizes scheduling decisions and observable task state
Allows scheduler and execution components to be deployed separately
costs: The metadata database is a coordination dependency and capacity boundary
Scheduler decisions can lag when parsing, database, or executor work is backlogged

features.name: Pluggable executor boundary
features.description: Airflow exposes a common executor interface so task instances can run locally in the scheduler process or be sent to remote worker and container systems.
benefits: Separates DAG scheduling from deployment-specific task execution
Offers a trade-off between low latency, isolation, and scaling
costs: Executor selection changes resource, latency, and failure behavior
Remote executors add queueing and infrastructure dependencies

features.name: Separated DAG processing and task execution
features.description: Airflow 3 separates DAG processing from the scheduler and API server, while workers receive task execution requests and access the selected DAG bundle version.
benefits: Reduces the scheduler's direct exposure to DAG author code
Permits component-specific scaling and security boundaries
costs: Multiple component boundaries create synchronization and deployment complexity
DAG bundle versioning affects whether processors and workers observe the same definition

mathematical_views.question: How do task dependency edges and prior task-instance states determine which task instances are eligible for execution?
assumptions: The workflow graph is acyclic for each modeled DAG
Trigger rules and mapped-task details are abstracted into an eligibility predicate
A DAG run has a stable definition while the predicate is evaluated

lifecycle.notes: Candidate lifecycle model proposed from the cited DAG and scheduler evidence; trigger-rule and mapped-task assumptions remain outside this bounded assertion.

mathematical_views.question: How does the scheduler transform persisted DAG and task state into executor workloads and observed task outcomes?
assumptions: The metadata database is the shared state boundary for the modeled scheduler
Executor event reporting eventually reaches the scheduler
The view abstracts SQL transaction details and scheduler heartbeat timing

mathematical_views.question: Which workflow-level properties remain invariant when the same task workload is assigned to local, queued, or containerized executors?
assumptions: The executor honors the common task workload contract
Task code and dependencies are available in each execution environment
Latency, isolation, and failure semantics are allowed to differ between executors

costs: Graph complexity and acyclic constraints limit expression
Metadata storage and scheduler throughput become coordination bottlenecks

benefits: Deployment-specific execution without changing DAG semantics
costs: Executor choices trade latency, isolation, and operational cost

benefits: Stronger component isolation and independent scaling
costs: Version synchronization and multiple services add complexity
